text: {"content":"Keep protected events on the summary route when the new editor is enabled. With calendar.item.editInTab=true and calendar.event.createEditDialog.enabled=true, Details sends read-only events and invitations through modifyEventWithDialog. openEventDialog selects the summary URL and clears args.inTab, but this later condition then opens the new create/edit dialog.","codeSuggestion":"","assessment":"Required change. This condition already exists, but the new Details route exposes it for protected events. The preference defaults to false, so the normal test run misses the failure.","rationale":"The condition checks mode === \"modify\" without preserving the earlier calendar-writability and isEditable decisions. This violates the patch's protected-event contract. The new dialog does not restore those permission checks.","recommendation":"change","validation":"The existing native test times out in test_detailsDoesNotEditReadOnlyEvent when run with --setpref=calendar.event.createEditDialog.enabled=true. The same test passes with the default preference. A dispatch experiment using the actual function confirms the incorrect route for both read-only events and invitations.","appliedSummary":"","changeSummary":"Preserve the summary route for protected events before selecting the new create/edit dialog.
